title: Catalog Debut Passport: Coordinated Ops & Release Checklist for New Model
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Purpose: run a tight, cross-functional launch for a new model entry in the public catalog. This ticket bundles the pre-launch checklist, release notes coordination, benchmark validation, docs publication, and announcement sequencing. Goal: ship the model to catalog with clear performance claims, up-to-date docs, coordinated comms, and rollback criteria. Assumptions: model artifact has been validated by Applied ML; serving permutations (quantized / fp16 / cpu) will be published incrementally; Dedicated and Private availability require separate release gates (tracked in dependencies).
acceptance_criteria: Model tile appears in catalog with metadata (size, license, recommended configs)
Benchmark suite results published (latency P50/P95, throughput, quality eval snapshots) and linked in the model page
Release notes drafted and approved by PM + Legal + Security
Docs (API examples, SDK snippets, migration notes) published in docs.redwood.ai and referenced in catalog card
Announcement copy approved and scheduled across blog, changelog, product newsletter, & social channels
Rollout plan includes fallback policies and a defined rollback signal set (latency spike, error rate > threshold, quality regression)
tasks: Confirm final model artifact and version tag from Research: gs://redwood-models/v2.3.1 (ENG-22844)
Run full benchmark harness and collect perf/quality: latency P50/P95, token cost, eval suite pass rates
Draft model metadata (size, quantization guidance, recommended hardware) for catalog card
Write release notes: short summary, breaking changes (if any), migration steps
Update SDK examples (Python/Node) and add structured output example where applicable
Create docs page: How to choose this model vs alternatives, cost/perf tradeoffs
Design review: model card visual, iconography, and badge set (DES-4101)
Legal review: license verification and export controls
Security review: verify no sensitive data leakage in training artifacts
QA: smoke test model via hosted API and Dedicated preview pool
PRs: create markdown release notes and docs PRs, link GH PRs here
Comms: prepare blog draft, changelog entry, newsletter blurb, social snippets
Schedule rollout windows per region & capacity constraints
Run preflight checklist 48h before publish and sign-off by PM, Eng, Design, Legal
rollout_timeline: 2026-03-10: Soft publish to internal catalog + Dedicated preview cluster (invite-only)
2026-03-12: Public catalog card staged (no announcement), docs PR merged to staging
2026-03-15 09:00 PDT: Final preflight review (PM/Eng/Design/Legal/Security) - signoff required
2026-03-16 14:00 PDT: Public catalog publish (model visible in UI) + release notes live
2026-03-16 16:00 PDT: Blog + changelog + newsletter + social posts go live (coordinated)
2026-03-16 to 2026-03-23: Monitoring window — increased telemetry retention and alert thresholds lowered for early detection
post_launch_monitoring: Key metrics dashboard link: https://dashboard.redwood.ai/d/catalogn/pm-99750 (observe latency P50/P95, errors, token cost)
Alert thresholds: error rate > 1% for 30m, latency P95 > baseline + 200ms for 15m, quality eval regression > 3 points
Customer signal: watch top-5 active customers for increased error/latency; DR team to contact any with impacted SLAs
Logs & traces retention increased to 30d for the first week
Run labeled prompt tests (50 representative prompts) daily for first 7 days to detect quality drift

risks_mitigations: Risk: Performance regression after publish. Mitigation: keep canary pool and immediate rollback button; pre-defined rollback criteria in release notes.
Risk: Legal flags on dataset provenance. Mitigation: include conservative language and delay publish if legal sign-off not received.
Risk: Dedicated capacity shortage in APAC. Mitigation: stagger Dedicated availability by region and include fallback to hosted variant in catalog card.
